1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicants; learned Aga for opposite party no.1, learned counsel for
the informant and perused the material placed on record.

2.  The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed by the applicants to quash the impugned summoning order dated 09.02.2024 as well as entire proceeding of Complaint Case No.331 of 2024 (Sujata Vs. Kushal Gupta & others), under Sections 419, 420, 406, 323, 376, 504, 506 IPC, Police Station Baghwala, District Etah, pending in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Etah,
District Etah.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

District Etah
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that the applicant no.2 is the resident of Dubai,
UAE (United Arab Emirat).
The present complaint has been filed after four and half years of the incident.
No plausible explanation has been given about this delay.
It is further submitted that no medical report has been brought on record.
The applicants never met the victim nor made any promise to provide job in Dubai.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra learned AGA and learned counsel for the informant have opposed the prayer and submitted that witnesses and other persons have seen the incident of commission of rape.
The statement of the victim recorded under Section 200 Cr.P.C. and of her witneses recorded under Section 202 Cr.P.C. have duly supported the version of the prosecution.
The summoning order has been passed on the basis of the primary evidence.
5. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and after going through the material available on record, the prayer made by the applicants, is refused.

6. However, it is provided that in case the applicants apply for bail within a period of 30 days from today, their application for bail shall be considered and disposed of expeditiously in view of law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825.
7.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For a period of 30 days from today or till the applicants surrender and apply for bail, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants in the aforesaid case.
8. With the aforesaid observations, the present application is finally disposed of.
